draft.title: Judging historical significance
card: Historians do not study everything from the past. They choose events and people that were significant, meaning they mattered a great deal in history.
Three tests help. How many people were affected? How long did the effects last? Did it change how people lived and thought?
The printing press passes all three. It spread books and ideas to many people in Europe, its effects lasted for centuries, and it changed how people learned and thought.
Significance is a judgement. Something can matter a lot to a few people for a short time and still be less significant overall.
draft.remember: Ask how many, how long and how much change.

a.q: Which description best shows that an event was historically significant?
opts: It changed the lives of millions of people for centuries
It was recorded in detail by one writer at the time
It happened a very long time ago
It was dramatic and surprising for those who saw it
a.why: Many people affected and lasting effects are two of the three tests. Being old or dramatic does not make an event significant, and one detailed record does not show wide or lasting effects.
a.clue: Think about how many people were affected and for how long.

b.q: A town in Tasmania held a famous fair in 1850 that drew big crowds for one weekend. A new law that year gave all children in the colony the right to attend school, and it shaped education for generations. Which is more significant, and why?
opts: The law, because it had wide and lasting effects
The fair, because it drew big crowds in one place
The fair, because many people remembered it fondly
The law, because laws are always more significant than fairs
b.why: The law affected many children and its effects lasted for generations, and it changed how people lived. The fair drew crowds, but only briefly. The last option fails because significance depends on effects, not on the type of event.
b.clue: Compare how long each one affected people.

a.best: It changed the lives of millions of people for centuries

b.best: The law, because it had wide and lasting effects

problems.detail: The scenario gives a real place and date as if real. In 1850 the colony was Van Diemen's Land: it was officially renamed Tasmania in 1856. Also, no 1850 law gave all children there the right to attend school. Tasmania's compulsory schooling law came in 1868. Students could learn a false fact. Make the example clearly invented, or use a real event.

The option 'The law, because laws are always more significant than fairs' uses 'always', while the card frames significance as a judgement with 'can'. It is a distractor, but the absolute wording is flagged as required.
